input.why: Triple puff held to toggle crouch is their dominant choice for this exact job, used in 17 of 35 games (49%), far ahead of the next option at 9%.
Right-center sip is used for camera-reset/lock-on in 22 of 32 games combined across tap timings, and tap 200 alone leads at 41% (13/32).
Right puff held briefly is their top pick for guard/block-type actions, used in 15 of 39 games (38%), well ahead of the next option at 18%.
Center sip toggle is their clear top choice for this ability-slot type job, used in 19 of 41 games (46%), nearly double the next option.
Triple sip is their leading choice for dodge/dash-type actions, used in 14 of 37 games (38%), well clear of the next option at 14%.

Soft right sip is used for this item-use job in 13 of 34 games (38%), and their other three ranked options all use the same input, showing strong consensus on the sensor even before the function detail.
Soft triple sip is their top pick for this interact/pickup-type action, used in 14 of 35 games (40%), well ahead of the next option at 17%.

This job is fragmented across their history (top two options tied at 13%), but mp_left_sip matches the breath-based pattern they use for the other three loadout-switch controls in this same profile (dpad_E, dpad_N, dpad_S all use sip/puff variants), so it stays consistent with that family rather than the tied 'W' entry, which only appears in a game with a physical D-pad control scheme.
Soft left sip is their leading choice for this weapon/loadout-switch job, used in 12 of 33 games (36%), ahead of the next option at 12%.
Soft right-center sip tapped is their dominant choice for switching an equipped ability, used in 12 of 28 games (43%), far ahead of the next option at 11%.
Soft right puff is their top pick for switching a consumable/item slot, used in 8 of 30 games (27%), ahead of a three-way tie at 10% for the rest.
Soft left puff is their leading choice for opening the main menu, used in 13 of 33 games (39%), ahead of the same input with a delay at 24%.
Soft right sip held is their single most-used binding for opening a map, used in 7 of 32 games (22%), the top-ranked entry for this job.

input.summary: Settled 13 of 17 real Elden Ring controls from clear majorities in their own history (crouch, lock-on, guard, skill, dodge, item use, interact, weapon/spell/item switching, menu, map). Asked 4 questions on controls where their history splits close to evenly between genuinely different playstyles: forward/backward movement (breath-latch vs joystick tilt) and light/strong attack (which mouth action to use). Left the 13 keyboard/mouse rows unbound since they have no established function in Elden Ring and every needed action is already covered by the mapped controller outputs, so no token was guessed for them.
